title: 19WA8026Q0036 - Janitorial services at Embassy office building and Warehouse.
description: The U.S. Embassy in Windhoek hereby provides the following solicitation notice in respect of the issuance of a Request for Quotation (RFQ) for: Janitorial/cleaning services at the U.S. Embassy Office building and General services warehouse in Windhoek, Namibia. title: Progressive Design-Build (PDB) - RENOVATE HQ AFMC B/10262 PH 2 at WPAFB
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) is issuing this special notice to announce an upcoming competition for a construction solicitation for the Air Force Materiel Command (AFMC) Headquarters (HQ) Renovation, Building 10262, utilizing an Other Transaction (OT) Agreement under 10 U.S.C. � 2808a. The anticipated delivery method is Progressive Design-Build (PDB). This notice is for informational and planning purposes. INDUSTRY DAY USACE intends to conduct an Industry Day on 03 December 2026 at 0900 Eastern Time to provide an overview of the project, acquisition strategy, and anticipated requirements. This event will provide interested parties with an opportunity to gain additional insight into the project and proposed PDB under an OT (non-FAR-based) framework. A notional acquisition schedule will be shared. Interested parties are encouraged to ask questions and provide input in advance of the official Request for Qualifications (RFQ) release. General questions will be permitted during the Industry Day; however, all discussions and responses provided during the event are considered unofficial and are for informational purposes only. Statements made during the Industry Day do not constitute commitment, authorization, or binding guidance related to the future RFQ. Official Questions and Answers (Q&A) will be accepted and addressed following the release of RFQ. LOCATION Industry Day Presentation location: Hope Hotel, 10823 Chidlaw Rd # A, Dayton, OH 45433 PROJECT OVERVIEW Project Title: Renovate Headquarters (HQ) Air Force Materiel Command (AFMC), Building 10262, Phase 2 Construction Location: Wright-Patterson Air Force Base (WPAFB), OH Agency: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Louisville District NAICS Code: 236220 PROJECT DESCRIPTION This acquisition will deliver the design and construction for the progressive design-build phased renovation of Building 10262, AFMC HQ, at WPAFB, OH. The scope of work consists of furnishing all necessary equipment, materials, labor, supervision, quality control, and supplies to deliver a fully functional, modernized headquarters facility while supporting ongoing occupied command operations. Key features of the project may include: Facility Renewal, Envelope, and Interior Renovation: Replacement of the Building 10262 roof and related envelope work, comprehensive interior renovation and finishes of the entire second floor, designated basement areas, required building repairs, and hazardous-material abatement. Critical Infrastructure Overhaul: Modernization and replacement of affected mechanical, electrical, plumbing (MEP), heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC), electric-power, telecommunications, fire-protection, fire-alarm, and life-safety systems necessary to support the renovated areas. Secure Facilities & Specialized Spaces: Turnkey design, construction, and Defense Intelligence Agency (DIA) accreditation of Special Access Program (SAP) and Sensitive Compartmented Information Facility (SCIF) spaces compliant with ICD 705 / IC Tech Spec and DoDM 5205.07 Vol 3 standards (including designated basement areas). Occupied Facility Logistics & Continuity: Construction sequencing, utility/system outage planning, temporary bypass systems, controlled access, and strict coordination to maintain uninterrupted global command operations supporting approximately 4,000 personnel. ACQUISITION STRATEGY � PRE-AWARD USACE � Louisville District will use a streamlined competitive selection process: Step 1 � RFQ: Interested parties will submit a Statement of Qualifications (SOQ). Following evaluation of the qualification packages, the Government intends to short-list a target of three (3) of the highest qualified Design-Builders to proceed to Step 2. Step 2 � Pitch Presentations: Short-listed firms must attend a mandatory site visit at WPAFB, OH during pitch preparation, followed by live, interactive presentations. Problem-solving, technical approach, risk management, and team chemistry will be evaluated by the Government. Step 3 � Exclusive Negotiation: Based on pitch evaluations, the Government will select one Design-Builder to enter exclusive negotiations. All interested parties should monitor the official solicitation announcement, which will provide complete details and submission instructions. Draft documents may be provided at a future date for feedback and informational purposes only and are subject to change upon issuance of the formal project RFQ. Virtual Participation Opportunity: For those who are unable to attend the Industry Day event in person, the Louisville District will also make the event available via Microsoft Teams. The details related to the MS Teams event are provided below: Microsoft Teams Meeting Join: https://dod.teams.microsoft.us/meet/993610255621?p=yaQ28DL3lmCC9Nap5C Meeting ID: 993 610 255 621 Passcode: Y6sB764r This is a combined Industry Day for AFMC and United States Space Force (USSF).

title: Saltash Guildhall Internal Works
description: Saltash Town Council is seeking tenders from suitably qualified contractors for internal remodelling works at the Guildhall, Lower Fore Street, Saltash. The project comprises refurbishment and adaptation works to support revised council operations and meeting functions, including: Manufacture and installation of bespoke horseshoe-shaped council chamber desking accommodating approximately 20 members/users. Supply and installation of audio visual equipment to support hybrid meetings, Microsoft Teams connectivity, microphones, displays, speakers and associated control systems. Installation of an assisted listening system. Electrical alterations and new power and data infrastructure within the First Floor Long Room. Electrical and data alterations within the Ground Floor Council Chamber. Electrical and data alterations within the Clerk's Office. Heating alterations including replacement radiators within the Council Chamber. Supply and installation of acoustic underlay and new carpet finishes within the First Floor Long Room. Associated commissioning, testing, certification, training and making good. The works will be undertaken within an occupied civic building and contractors must maintain safe operation of the premises throughout the contract period.

title: Marketplace for Acquisition of Professional Services (MAPS)
description: Army Contracting Command-Aberdeen Proving Ground (ACC-APG), in support of the Capability Program Executive (CPE) Enterprise Software and Service (ES2) (formerly known as Program Executive Office (PEO) Enterprise), intends to award a Multiple Award (MA) Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract, MAPS. This is the follow-on and combination of the ACC-APG Responsive Strategic Sourcing for Services (RS3) and Product Lead (PL) Digital Market�s Information Technology Enterprise Solutions � 3 Services (ITES-3S) IDIQ Contract Vehicles. The objective of the MAPS IDIQ contract is to provide Army customers, Portfolio Acquisition Executives (PAE), CPEs, Department of War (DoW) agencies, and other federal agencies with uncommon knowledge-based professional services and support the Army enterprise infrastructure and infostructure goals with information technology (IT) services worldwide (inside the contiguous United States (CONUS) and outside the contiguous United States (OCONUS)), including hostile areas. By combining these vehicles, the Army aims to enhance flexibility, reduce redundancy, and improve cost-efficiency in acquiring uncommon knowledge-based professional services. This integration will also ensure a unified approach in meeting the Army�s evolving technology and strategic needs, thus optimizing mission readiness and effectiveness. title: R799--Lake Baldwin EUL Development Opportunity Sources Sought COR: Dustin Koonce
description: Lake Baldwin VA Clinic, FL EUL Request for Expressions of Interest 1 REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST ENHANCED-USE LEASE DEVELOPMENT OPPORTUNITY Orlando Healthcare System Veterans Integrated Service Network 08 (VISN 08) Lake Baldwin VA Medical Clinic - Orlando, FL Notice This advertisement is a notice of a potential opportunity. This Request for Expressions of Interest (the advertisement ) is not a solicitation for offers, nor is it a request for proposals. Respondents are advised that the Government assumes no responsibility to award an Enhanced-Use Lease (EUL) based upon responses to this advertisement. This Sources Sought Notice is to identify potential sources for information and planning purposes only and is not intended to pre-qualify or disqualify any potential Respondents. The purpose of this Sources Sought is to conduct market research to determine if there are responsible and qualified entities interested in redeveloping the assets described in Section III and if yes, what potential reuse options exist. The information gained from this Sources Sought will be used to assist the Government in determining if this development opportunity can be competitive and/or a total Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) or Veteran-Owned Small Business (VOSB) Set-Aside. The Government will use this information to determine the best acquisition strategy for this procurement and to inform related asset management decision-making. The Government requests that interested parties respond to this Notice with the specific information requested in Section V of this Notice and identify their small business status. VA is particularly interested in SDVOSB/VOSB respondents capabilities to perform a minimum of 51% of the development opportunity described in this Notice. Developers responding to this market research should be aware that responding to this advertisement may not ensure that they qualify for any underlying future solicitation or contract award. Responding to this Sources Sought Notice is NOT a prerequisite to respond to any future subsequent solicitations. The Government will not reimburse participants for any expenses associated with their participation in this Sources Sought. The Government cannot provide any warranty, expressed or implied, as to the accuracy, reliability or completeness of the information contained in this Notice. Overview and Objectives The United States Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), under its Enhanced-Use Leasing (EUL) authority (38 U.S.C. §§ 8161- 8169, as amended), is seeking expressions of interest from qualified developers, including SDVOSBs and VOSBs, to serve as a Developer for purposes of developing supportive housing or other uses that directly or indirectly benefit Veterans (e.g., general affordable housing, skilled nursing facilities, technical job training centers, research facilities, mixed-use, other). VA s EUL authority allows VA to outlease land and improvements to selected developers (i.e., Lessees) to provide housing and/or other uses that directly or indirectly benefit Veterans. Such leases can have a term of up to 99 years. VA s Office of Asset Enterprise Management (OAEM) administers the EUL Program. An EUL is a long-term ground lease of underutilized VA-owned land or buildings to a non-federal entity (Developer). Under the EUL program, the Developer secures a long-term leasehold interest with VA for the subject property. This deal structure enables developers to finance, design, develop, renovate/construct, operate, and maintain improvements on VA property to directly or indirectly benefit Veterans. The objective of this development opportunity is to repurpose assets at the Lake Baldwin VA Medical Clinic under VA s EUL Program to the benefit of Veterans. Respondents should consider the following as they formulate responses to this Notice: Lease-back by VA or other Federal government entities is not permissible, and financing cannot reflect a lease-back arrangement. The PACT Act does not nullify 38 U.S.C. § 8162(b)(5), which states, "The terms of an enhanced-use lease may not provide for any acquisition, contract, demonstration, exchange, grant, incentive, procurement, sale, other transaction authority, service agreement, use agreement, lease, or lease-back by the Secretary or Federal Government. VA may only receive cash consideration for ground lease rent in an EUL (per 38 U.S.C. § 8162(b)(3)(B)). This means VA cannot receive any in-kind consideration or free/discounted services as part of a new EUL agreement. However, projects may provide free or discounted services to individual Veterans or Veteran Service Organizations, and the Secretary may enter into an EUL without receiving consideration per U.S.C. § 8162(b)(3)(C). title: FWS - Pixley NWR Water Recirculation Design-Build
description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial services prepared in accordance with Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) Part 12, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes only solicitation. Offers are being requested, and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. The U.S. Fish & Wildlife Service, Pixley National Wildlife Refuge provides 755 acres of wetland habitat for migratory waterfowl and other water birds and relies on three deep groundwater wells for irrigation and flooding. This project will improve water reuse and reduce groundwater pumping demands, particularly during drought years. The contractor shall design and construct a water recirculation system consisting of approximately 1.2 miles of PVC pipeline connecting the wetlands� lowest topographical point to the existing pipeline farther east. The system shall include a pump at this low point to move water upslope for recirculation and critical irrigation. The contractor shall secure the pump station with a 12-foot-tall, gated chain-link enclosure topped with barbed wire. Excavated soil may be reused on refuge property, and restoration or seeding of disturbed ground will not be required. The construction magnitude is estimated to be between $700,000.00 to $750,000.00. title: Spain – Water-treatment chemicals – Suministro de reactivos para la potabilización del agua en las Estaciones de Tratamiento de Aguas Potables (ETAP) que gestiona Aguas de Córdoba-EMPROACSA mediante sistema dinámico de adquisición
description: Las diferentes Estaciones de Tratamiento de Agua Potable ETAP gestionadas por Aguas de Córdoba-EMPROACSA necesitan del suministro continuado de diferentes productos químicos a fin de garantizar el apropiado tratamiento y, por tanto, la salubridad del agua para poder cumplir con los parámetros exigidos por la normativa vigente para la potabilización del agua. Teniendo en cuenta la exhaustiva norma que regula la fabricación, transporte, descarga y dosificación de los productos empleados en la potabilización del agua de consumo humano y la necesidad permanente de suministro de tales productos, se hace necesaria la contratación de los mismos con empresas especializadas y que reúnan los requerimientos normativos exigidos para garantizar la salubridad del agua de consumo humano. La modalidad de contratación que se propone, a través de sistema dinámico de adquisición, nace de la necesidad de mejorar los tiempos de respuesta a determinadas necesidades de la organización.

title: DA01--Veterans Health Information Systems and Technology (VISTA) Blood Establishment Computer Software (VBECS) Operations and Maintenance Support II
description: VA is seeking sources that are able to provide full lifecycle sustainment and operational support, and any associated bug/fix development, and regulatory compliance services for the VA s existing Veterans Health Administration s VBECS, an FDA regulated Class II Medical Device Software product. The Contractor will be required to plan, manage, develop bug/fixes, test, deploy, maintain, document, and continuously monitor the VBECS system throughout the DevOps lifecycle. The Contractor will be required to maintain all system related documentation, ensuring accuracy, traceability, and compliance with FDA Quality System Regulations (21 CFR 820), ISO 13485:2016, and VA cybersecurity and privacy requirements. The Contractor will be required to support all activities required to maintain the VBECS s existing Authority to Operate, including preparation, validation, and submission of documentation within the SNOW Continuous Authorization and Monitoring environment, and continuous support for audits, assessments, and security reviews.

title: Remedial Investigation (RI) and Optional Feasibility Study (FS) for Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances (PFAS), Former Fort Ord, Monterey County, California
description: This Sources Sought Notice is for Market Research ONLY to determine the availability, capability and interest of small business firms for a potential small business category type set-aside. NO AWARD will be made from this Sources Sought Notice. NO SOLICITATION, SPECIFICATIONS, OR DRAWINGS ARE AVAILABLE AT THIS TIME as this is solely for Market Research. Please do not request such documentation. Requests for any of this information will go unanswered. If the conditions at Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO)19.104-1(a) are met the contracting officer is required to set the acquisition aside for small business concerns. Accordingly, interested contractors who have the skill, capabilities, and workload capacity to complete the described project (either through self-performance and/or the managing of subcontractors) are invited to provide their capability statements to the point of contact listed below. All responses will be used to determine the appropriate acquisition strategy for a potential acquisition. The purpose of this notice is to obtain a snapshot of current market capabilities and gain knowledge of potential small business sources to include small business in the following socioeconomic categories: Certified HUB Zone; Woman-Owned Small Business (WOSB) and Serviced-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB); Veteran Owned Small Business (VOSB) and 8(a) small business concerns to perform database updates to increase the capabilities, usability, and stability of currently existing applications. Other than small business are encouraged to express interest and submit capability statements as well. Contractors� capabilities will be reviewed solely for the purpose of determining an appropriate acquisition strategy to include whether this prospective action is appropriate to be set-aside for the small business community or should proceed as an unrestricted full and open acquisition. Other than small businesses are encouraged to respond to this NOTICE to provide a greater context of current market capabilities. However, per the Federal Acquisition Regulations, preference will be given to the small business categories as listed above. In determining the acquisition strategy, the Government must ensure there is adequate competition among the potential pool of available contractors. The Government intends to award a Firm Fixed Price order with a Period of Performance of five (5) years from date of award. An estimated solicitation date has not yet been determined. The NAICS Code is 562910, Environmental Remediation Services. The Size Standard in Number of Employees: 1,000 Employees. Product Service Code is B510. GENERAL SCOPE: Regulatory & Data Governance Regulatory Framework: This Base Realignment and Closure (BRAC) site is governed by the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act (CERCLA) in which the work must strictly adhere to the developed Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances (PFAS) Remedial Investigation (RI) Quality Assurance Project Plan (QAPP) which utilizes the Uniform Federal Policy for Quality Assurance Project Plans (UFP-QAPP). The Contractor must transmit all documents and data via Fort Ord Data Information Site (FODIS). All actions are dictated by the Federal Facilities Agreement (FFA) with the regulatory community. The Contractor will anticipate significant comments on products generated for this effort and must present technically competent PFAS subject matter experts to address and resolve comments suitable for public consumption per EPA Risk Communication guidelines. The Contractor must demonstrate past experience executing CERCLA work under an active FFA alongside USACE, U.S. Army BRAC, U.S. EPA, California DTSC, and California Regional Water Quality Control Boards. Compliance Standards: All analyses must be conducted by Department of Defense (DoD) Environmental Laboratory Accreditation Program (ELAP)-accredited laboratories per DoD Quality Systems Manual (QSM) Table B-15 using DoD Module 3 data validation with Fort Ord Data Information Site (FODIS) upload and follow safety compliance per U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Engineer Manual (EM) 385-1-1 via an Accident Prevention Plan (APP) and Site Safety and Health Plan (SSHP). Technical & Key Personnel Qualifications: The Contractor must present an overview of qualified in-house staff or primary teaming partners (e.g., Professional Geologists/Hydrogeologists registered in California, Environmental Engineers with water treatment optimization expertise, Quality Assurance Chemists, and USACE EM 385-1-1 Certified Safety Professionals) and show the ability to identified commercial analytical laboratories possessing active DoD ELAP accreditation for PFAS analysis by LC/MS/MS compliant with DoD QSM criteria. 2. Field Characterization and Waste Management Subsurface Drilling: Per the PFAS RI QAPP, the Contractor must advance continuous soil borings advanced to groundwater (~100 feet below ground surface [bgs]) with discrete depth-interval profiling, conduct the installation of multi-cased wells per the Drilling, American Society for Testing and Materials (ASTM) D5092 construction, and conduct multi-aquifer development including shallow water table (~100 ft bgs), intermediate Upper 180-Foot Aquifer (~225 ft bgs), and deep Seaside Groundwater Basin (up to 500 ft bgs). Groundwater Monitoring: Per the PFAS RI QAPP, the Contractor must conduct baseline, seasonal, and base wide sampling rounds for plume delineation. The Contractor will be expected to have an advanced understanding of the areas subsurface hydrology given the Salinas-Valley Aquitard and its various discontinuities as influenced by local potable water and agricultural pumping variations and inform the Government on modifications to the existing MODFLOW model. The Contractor will be expected to operate and maintain existing multi-well port systems in monitoring wells. Strict PFAS Sampling Cross-Contamination Mitigation: Per the PFAS RI QAPP the Contractor must adhere to strict avoidance of PFAS-containing field equipment, bailers, tubing, pumps, personal protective equipment (PPE), decontamination reagents, sunscreens, and vehicle materials and of documented PFAS Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and field blank / equipment rinsate validation programs. Investigation-Derived Waste (IDW) Protocols: The Contractor must be proficient at handling, containment, characterization, transportation, and disposal/destruction of PFAS-impacted drill cuttings, purge water, development water, and decontamination fluids in strict accordance with DoD and State of California regulations. 3. Specialized Comparative Studies HydraSleeve vs. Low-Flow: Per the PFAS RI QAPP the Contractor must demonstrate competency in the described field study assessing data quality, bias, and operational efficacy for PFAS passive sampling versus conventional purge techniques. The Contractor must demonstrate the ability to evaluate data comparability, turbidity impacts, sampling precision/accuracy, and relative bias for both short- and long-chain perfluoroalkyl and polyfluoroalkyl substances, and past experience designing, executing, and reporting side-by-side comparative studies between passive sampling devices (specifically HydraSleeve) and conventional low-flow (minimal drawdown) purging/sampling techniques. Granular Activated Carbon (GAC) Plant Efficacy: The Contractor must evaluate influent, mid-bed, and effluent monitoring campaigns across multiple Groundwater Treatment System (GWTS) facilities for short- and long-chain PFAS removal kinetics and plant optimization comingled with co-contaminants. The Contractor must demonstrate technical capability conducting Granular Activated Carbon (GAC) bench-, pilot-, or full-scale efficacy evaluations targeting PFAS breakthrough and mass removal kinetics with preferred experience evaluating and optimizing existing pump-and-treat groundwater treatment plants (GWTPs) for PFAS removal across carbon be

description: ISBEE Set-Aside � Advanced Practice Provider Physician Assistant/Nurse Practitioner Services Solicitation No. 75H70627Q00018 This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial services prepared in accordance with the HHS-adopted FAR Part 12, as supplemented by the attached solicitation documents. This announcement and its attachments constitute the solicitation. Quotations are requested, and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation No. 75H70627Q00018 is issued as a Request for Quotation (RFQ) for Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP), non-personal Advanced Practice Provider (APP) Physician Assistant (PA) and/or Nurse Practitioner (NP) healthcare services at Rosebud IHS Hospital, Rosebud, South Dakota. The Great Plains Area Indian Health Service (IHS) seeks a Contractor to provide qualified APP personnel sufficient to support two (2) full-time equivalent PA and/or NP positions providing outpatient primary care services at the Rosebud IHS Hospital Outpatient Department Clinic. Services include adult and pediatric primary care, chronic disease management, preventive and wellness services, acute outpatient care, authorized minor procedures, clinical documentation, referrals, care coordination, and quality-improvement activities. The Contractor shall furnish qualified licensed personnel, management, supervision, credentialing and privileging support, licensure and certification maintenance, professional liability insurance, staffing continuity, replacement personnel, and other Contractor-furnished resources necessary to perform the Performance Work Statement (PWS). This acquisition is set aside exclusively for Indian Small Business Economic Enterprises (ISBEEs). The assigned NAICS code is 561320, Temporary Help Services, with a small business size standard of $34.0 million in average annual receipts. Quoters shall satisfy the applicable ISBEE eligibility and representation requirements and submit the completed IHS Indian Economic Enterprise Representation form with their quotations. The anticipated award is a Firm-Fixed-Price, non-personal healthcare services purchase order using a Month-of-Service (MOS) pricing structure. One (1) MOS represents complete monthly performance of the required APP services, including qualified staffing equivalent to two (2) full-time PAs or NPs, scheduled outpatient clinic services, clinical documentation, care coordination, required training, and all other PWS requirements. The anticipated period of performance consists of a three (3)-month base period and three (3) option periods of three (3) months each, for a maximum potential period of performance of twelve (12) months. The anticipated base period is February 1, 2027, through April 30, 2027. Option-period dates will be specified in the resulting purchase order. Services will be performed at the Rosebud IHS Hospital Outpatient Department Clinic, 800 Hospital Drive, Rosebud, South Dakota 57570. Standard outpatient clinic hours are Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., excluding federal holidays, subject to the scheduling requirements identified in the PWS. Section F of the attached solicitation identifies the Contract Line Item Numbers (CLINs), service descriptions, quantities, units of measure, and performance periods. Quoters shall complete the price schedule with firm-fixed monthly MOS pricing for the base period and each option period. The Total Evaluated Price will include the base period and all three option periods. Award will be made to the responsible quoter whose quotation conforms to the solicitation requirements and represents the best value to the Government. Evaluation factors are Technical Capability and Management Approach, Past Performance, and Price. When combined, the non-price factors are significantly more important than Price. The Government intends to make a selection from initial quotations but reserves the right to request clarification, additional information, or revised quotations when determined appropriate. Questions must be received no later than 12:00 p.m. (noon) Central Standard Time (CST) on November 20, 2026. Quotations must be received no later than 12:00 p.m. (noon) CST on November 30, 2026. Submit questions and quotations electronically to David.Jones@ihs.gov, referencing RFQ No. 75H70627Q00018 � Rosebud APP Services in the email subject line. Quoters must have a valid Unique Entity Identifier (UEI), current System for Award Management (SAM) registration, and satisfy all applicable eligibility, responsibility, and exclusion requirements before award. Applicable solicitation provisions and contract clauses are identified in the attached Provisions and Clauses schedule. Prospective quoters are responsible for reviewing the complete solicitation package, including the Combined Synopsis/Solicitation, PWS and addendum, price schedule, quotation instructions, evaluation criteria, applicable FAR/HHSAR provisions and clauses, IHS Indian Economic Enterprise Representation form, and any amendments before submitting a quotation.

description: This Sources Sought Notice is for Market Research ONLY to determine the availability, capability and interest of small business firms for a potential small business category type set-aside. NO AWARD will be made from this Sources Sought Notice. NO SOLICITATION, SPECIFICATIONS, OR DRAWINGS ARE AVAILABLE AT THIS TIME as this is solely for Market Research. Please do not request such documentation. Requests for any of this information will go unanswered. If the conditions at Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO)19.104-1(a) are met the contracting officer is required to set the acquisition aside for small business concerns. Accordingly, interested contractors who have the skill, capabilities, and workload capacity to complete the described project (either through self-performance and/or the managing of subcontractors) are invited to provide their capability statements to the point of contact listed below. All responses will be used to determine the appropriate acquisition strategy for a potential acquisition. The purpose of this notice is to obtain a snapshot of current market capabilities and gain knowledge of potential small business sources to include small business in the following socioeconomic categories: Certified HUB Zone; Woman-Owned Small Business (WOSB) and Serviced-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB); Veteran Owned Small Business (VOSB) and 8(a) small business concerns to perform database updates to increase the capabilities, usability, and stability of currently existing applications. Other than small business are encouraged to express interest and submit capability statements as well. Contractors� capabilities will be reviewed solely for the purpose of determining an appropriate acquisition strategy to include whether this prospective action is appropriate to be set-aside for the small business community or should proceed as an unrestricted full and open acquisition. Other than small businesses are encouraged to respond to this NOTICE to provide a greater context of current market capabilities. However, per the Federal Acquisition Regulations, preference will be given to the small business categories as listed above. In determining the acquisition strategy, the Government must ensure there is adequate competition among the potential pool of available contractors. The Government intends to award a Firm Fixed Price order with a Period of Performance of five (5) years from date of award. An estimated solicitation date has not yet been determined. The NAICS Code is 562910, Environmental Remediation Services. The Size Standard in Number of Employees: 1,000 Employees. Product Service Code is B510. GENERAL SCOPE: Regulatory & Data Governance Regulatory Framework: This Base Realignment and Closure (BRAC) site is governed by the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act (CERCLA) in which the work must strictly adhere to the developed Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances (PFAS) Remedial Investigation (RI) Quality Assurance Project Plan (QAPP) which utilizes the Uniform Federal Policy for Quality Assurance Project Plans (UFP-QAPP). The Contractor must transmit all documents and data via Fort Ord Data Information Site (FODIS). All actions are dictated by the Federal Facilities Agreement (FFA) with the regulatory community. The Contractor will anticipate significant comments on products generated for this effort and must present technically competent PFAS subject matter experts to address and resolve comments suitable for public consumption per EPA Risk Communication guidelines. The Contractor must demonstrate past experience executing CERCLA work under an active FFA alongside USACE, U.S. Army BRAC, U.S. EPA, California DTSC, and California Regional Water Quality Control Boards. Compliance Standards: All analyses must be conducted by Department of Defense (DoD) Environmental Laboratory Accreditation Program (ELAP)-accredited laboratories per DoD Quality Systems Manual (QSM) Table B-15 using DoD Module 3 data validation with Fort Ord Data Information Site (FODIS) upload and follow safety compliance per U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Engineer Manual (EM) 385-1-1 via an Accident Prevention Plan (APP) and Site Safety and Health Plan (SSHP). Technical & Key Personnel Qualifications: The Contractor must present an overview of qualified in-house staff or primary teaming partners (e.g., Professional Geologists/Hydrogeologists registered in California, Environmental Engineers with water treatment optimization expertise, Quality Assurance Chemists, and USACE EM 385-1-1 Certified Safety Professionals) and show the ability to identified commercial analytical laboratories possessing active DoD ELAP accreditation for PFAS analysis by LC/MS/MS compliant with DoD QSM criteria. 2. Field Characterization and Waste Management Subsurface Drilling: Per the PFAS RI QAPP, the Contractor must advance continuous soil borings advanced to groundwater (~100 feet below ground surface [bgs]) with discrete depth-interval profiling, conduct the installation of multi-cased wells per the Drilling, American Society for Testing and Materials (ASTM) D5092 construction, and conduct multi-aquifer development including shallow water table (~100 ft bgs), intermediate Upper 180-Foot Aquifer (~225 ft bgs), and deep Seaside Groundwater Basin (up to 500 ft bgs). Groundwater Monitoring: Per the PFAS RI QAPP, the Contractor must conduct baseline, seasonal, and base wide sampling rounds for plume delineation. The Contractor will be expected to have an advanced understanding of the areas subsurface hydrology given the Salinas-Valley Aquitard and its various discontinuities as influenced by local potable water and agricultural pumping variations and inform the Government on modifications to the existing MODFLOW model. The Contractor will be expected to operate and maintain existing multi-well port systems in monitoring wells. Strict PFAS Sampling Cross-Contamination Mitigation: Per the PFAS RI QAPP the Contractor must adhere to strict avoidance of PFAS-containing field equipment, bailers, tubing, pumps, personal protective equipment (PPE), decontamination reagents, sunscreens, and vehicle materials and of documented PFAS Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and field blank / equipment rinsate validation programs. title: MACH1_AOI_Military Working Dog Facility_ Vandenberg Space Force_LOE 1 and LOE 2
description: This Area of Interest (AOI) is published under the Modernized Agile Construction Horizons (MACH1) Umbrella Program Notice. All submissions must adhere to the procedures and guidelines outlined in the parent MACH1 framework document unless otherwise tailored herein. Any resulting agreement will be an Other Transaction Agreement (OTA) executed under the statutory authority of 10 U.S.C. � 2808a. The 772nd Enterprise Sourcing Squadron (772 ESS) is is executing a Progressive Design-Build (PDB) project to renovate existing military working dog (MWD) facilities and construct a new addition at Vandenberg Space Force Base (SFB), California. Under this agreement, the selected contractor will execute both the progressive design and physical construction to deliver a fully functional, code-compliant compound (Project Number: XUMU171121C). The current MWD kennel and admin facilities (Buildings 6444 and 6447) at Vandenberg SFB fail quarterly inspections and contain critical safety hazards that endanger military personnel and canine assets. title: ISBEE Solicitation: Emergency Department Registered Nurse Services (Up to 8 RNs) � Standing Rock Service Unit, Fort Yates IHS Hospital, Fort Yates, ND.
description: The Indian Health Service (IHS), Great Plains Area, is soliciting proposals for non-personal Emergency Department Registered Nurse services in support of the Standing Rock Service Unit, Fort Yates Hospital, Fort Yates, North Dakota, under Solicitation No. 75H70627R00002. The requirement is for up to eight (8) qualified Emergency Department Registered Nurse positions to support continuous 24-hour, 7-day-per-week Emergency Department operations. The anticipated contract type is Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP), commercial services, with one four (4)-month Base Period and fourteen (14) four-month Option Periods, for a total potential period of performance of sixty (60) months. This acquisition is set aside 100 percent for eligible Indian Small Business Economic Enterprises (ISBEEs) in accordance with the Buy Indian Act and applicable HHSAR requirements. The applicable NAICS code is 561320, Temporary Help Services, and the Product Service Code is Q401, Medical�Nursing. The Contractor will be responsible for providing qualified nursing personnel and all associated management, supervision, recruitment, credentialing, scheduling, replacement staffing, administrative support, and other resources necessary to perform the requirements of the Performance Work Statement. The requirement consists of up to eight (8) separately exercisable RN positions. The Base Period provides for up to eight (8) RN position CLINs, with the actual number of Base Period RN position CLINs awarded or funded identified in the resulting contract. During each Option Period, the Government may independently exercise from one (1) up to eight (8) RN position CLINs based on operational requirements and availability of funds. The Government is not obligated to award, fund, or exercise all eight RN positions, any particular RN position, or any Option Period. Pricing will be based on a common Firm-Fixed-Price RN Month of Service (RN/MOS) unit price for each performance period. The common RN/MOS unit price will apply uniformly to all RN positions within that performance period. The Total Evaluated Price will be based on the maximum potential requirement for the Base Period and all fourteen Option Periods; evaluation of all RN position CLINs and option prices does not obligate the Government to award, fund, or exercise all positions or options. Important Dates: Questions regarding the solicitation are due no later than November 13, 2026, at 12:00 p.m. Central Time. Proposals are due no later than November 30, 2026, at 12:00 p.m. Central Time. Award will be made using a Best Value Tradeoff process. Evaluation factors are Past Performance, Technical Approach, Management Approach, and Price. Past Performance, Technical Approach, and Management Approach, when combined, are more important than Price. Technical Approach and Management Approach will be evaluated using adjectival ratings of Outstanding, Good, Acceptable, Marginal, or Unacceptable. The Government may select a higher-priced proposal when the evaluated benefits of the non-price factors justify the associated price premium. Offerors are responsible for reviewing the complete solicitation package, including the Performance Work Statement, Price Schedule/Bid Sheet, applicable FAR/HHSAR provisions and clauses, Buy Indian Act/ISBEE representations, wage determination, and any amendments, prior to submitting an offer.

title: Department of War Pharmacy Uniform Formulary Blanket Purchase Agreement/Uniform Formulary Additional Discount Program
description: The Department of War (DoW) is required by law (10 U.S.C. � 1074g) to establish an effective, efficient, integrated pharmacy benefits program for the Military Health System (MHS) which includes the purchase pharmaceutical agents. The law and implementing regulation (32 CFR Section 199.21) describe the process by which the DoW Pharmacy and Therapeutics (P&T) Committee will consider the relative clinical effectiveness and relative cost effectiveness of pharmaceutical agents in a therapeutic class in recommending the selection of agents for the DoW Uniform Formulary (UF) and, for cost sharing purposes, the classification of a pharmaceutical agent as generic, formulary, Basic Core Formulary (BCF), Extended Core Formulary (ECF), or non-formulary (NF). Prior to the scheduled P&T Committee meeting, a Request for Quotation (RFQ) for pharmaceutical agents within Drug Classes identified for placement on the UF has been issued to obtain quotes from industry. The Defense Health Agency may award Uniform Formulary Blanket Purchase Agreements (UF BPA) and the Uniform Formulary Additional Discount Program Agreements (UF ADP) based on the UF decision. This process is described in the attached RFQ. P&T COMMITTEE MEETING: The following February 2027 newly approved drugs will be reviewed: Atebrioz � Skeletal Muscle Relaxants and Combinations � Subclass: NA Emcitate � Thyroid and Antithyroid Agents � Subclass: NA Hibsago � Hepatitis B Agents � Subclass: NA Juvmo � Parkinsons Agents � Subclass: NA Zegfrovy � Lung Cancer � Subclass: EGFR+ NSCLC The RFQ, including UF BPA and UF ADP appendices, are attached herein. description: This presolicitation notice is for an upcoming solicitation from the Southeast Regional Maintenance Center (SERMC) for Nonskid Removal and Replacement onboard U.S. Navy Ships and other vessels. The solicitation will be posted on SAM.gov on/after 30 October 2026. Nonskid application will be either MIL-PRF-24667 Type I or Type V roll-on nonskid, Type IV spray on nonskid, or Type XI peel and stick sections. title: Yuma Proving Ground Job Order Contract (JOC)
description: SOURCES SOUGHT SYNOPSIS Job Order Contract for Yuma Proving Ground This is a Sources Sought Synopsis (SSS) ONLY. This notice is issued solely for information and planning purposes � it does not constitute a Request for Quotation (RFQ), Invitation for Bid (IFB), or Request for Proposal (RFP) or a promise to issue an RFQ, IFB or RFP in the future. This notice does not commit the U.S. Government to contract for any supply or service. Further, the U.S. Government is not seeking quotes, bids or proposals at this time and will not accept unsolicited proposals in response to this sources sought synopsis. The U.S. Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this notice. Submittals will not be returned to the responder. Not responding to this notice does not preclude participation in any future RFQ, IFB, or RFP, if any is issued. If a solicitation is released, it will be synopsized on the Government wide Point of Entry (GPE). It is the responsibility of potential offerors to monitor the GPE for additional information pertaining to this requirement. The GPE is located at https://sam.gov. The United States (U.S.) Government desires to procure a Job Order Contract (JOC) at Yuma Proving Ground, on a small business set-aside basis, provided 2 or more qualified small businesses respond to this sources sought synopsis with information sufficient to support a set-aside. Be advised that the U.S. Government will not be able to set aside this requirement if two (2) or more small businesses do not respond with information to support the set-aside. We encourage all small businesses, in all socioeconomic categories (including, 8(a) Business Development Program, Small Disadvantage Business, Historically Underutilized Business Zone, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned, Women-Owned Small Business concerns), to identify their capabilities in meeting the requirement at a fair market price. BACKGROUND: A continuing need is anticipated for a job order contract at Yuma Proving Ground. Attached you will find the draft Statement of Work (SOW). The Government contract for these services was previously performed under contract W91151-21-D-0012. The Period of Performance ended 1 August 2026. The contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, supplies, facilities, transportation, tools, materials, supervision, and other items and construction services as defined in this SOW. The NAICS code for the requirement is 236220, Commercial and Institutional Building Construction with a corresponding size standard of $45 million. If your company believes a different NAICS code would better fit this requirement, please tell us your suggested NAICS and why it would better fit this requirement. The Contractor shall provide all supervision, labor, personnel, equipment, materials, and supplies, with the exception of Government Furnished Property (GFP), to perform activities under this Job Order Contract. PURPOSE OF THIS SOURCES SOUGHT: To request information on capabilities of potential offerors to provide the services described herein. Electronic submissions only: Responses are due no later than 13:00pm CDT on 30 November 2026 to facilitate planning and ensure maximum consideration. The email attachments cannot exceed 9 megabytes (MB) due to the Government�s email system restrictions. DO NOT SEND ZIPPED files as the Government�s network will remove all zipped files. Interested businesses should provide a brief capability statement package (limited to no more than 30 pages, single spaced, and 12 font size minimum) demonstrating specific capability in reference to this requirement. The Government prefers that your firm submits its response in Microsoft Word, Adobe Acrobat, or a combination of the two and the document(s) must be searchable. Include: Whether the experience has been as a prime contractor or subcontractor on similar requirements (include the services provided, the number of facilities involved, and any other relevant information you deem applicable). Email the capability package to: Marissa Joyner - Contract Specialist at email: Marissa.joyner.civ@army.mil and Andrew Graham - Contracting Officer at email: Andrew.s.graham6.civ@army.mil The email subject line should include: The Firm�s Name, �Response to the Sources Sought Synopsis for the JOC at Yuma Proving Ground, W5168W-26-R-A022". **Note: the location(s) and corresponding solicitation number that you are responding to must be identified on the subject line. In response to this sources sought, please provide: 1. A company�s profile must include: The name of the firm, point of contact, phone number, email address, number of employees, annual revenue history, CAGE code, and Unique Entity Identifier (UEI). number. Respondents must also indicate small business certification status, for example: Small Business (SB), Small Disadvantaged Business (SDB), 8(a), Economically Disadvantaged Woman Owned SB (EDWOSB), WOSB, HUBZone, or Service Disabled Veteran Owned SB (SDVOSB). 2. Respond to: What fundamental tasks you believe need to be performed to successfully accomplish the job order contract? In essence, what primary tasks should be used for determining minimum capability to provide these services? 3. Whether your firm is interested in competing for this requirement as a prime contractor. If you are subcontracting any of the services out, contemplating a Joint Venture, and/or creating a teaming arrangement, please provide the name of these companies and what work they will be performing, if available. Please provide your company�s specific experience in job order contracts and providing comparable services. Ensure the information is in sufficiently detailed regarding previous experience in managing job order contracts (indicate whether the experience has been as a prime contractor or subcontractor) on similar requirements (include the services provided, the number of facilities involved, and any other relevant information you deem applicable). If applicable, please provide the same experience information from any subcontracts, Joint Venture, and/or teaming partners you may propose with. 4. What percentage of work will be performed by the small business prime contractor and all similarly situated entity subcontractors? Note: In accordance with FAR 52.219-14 Limitations on Subcontracting (Oct 2022) and Class Deviation 2021-O0008, Revision 1 - Limitations on Subcontracting for Small Business (Feb 2023), for general construction under NAICS 236220, prime contractor and similarly situated subcontractors must perform at least 15% of the cost of the contract, excluding the cost of materials. 5. Type(s)/certifications(s) of proposed subcontractors (for example, SDB, 8(a), HUBZone, SDVOSB, or WOSB). 6. Information on the financial capacity of your business to meet financial obligations (i.e. payroll, payment of subcontractors, etc.). 7. How the Army can best structure these contract requirements to facilitate competition by and among small business concerns. 8. Identify any condition or action that may have the effect of unnecessarily restricting competition with respect to this acquisition. Please contact the MICC Advocate for Competition, Scott Kukes at email: scott.d.kukes.civ@army.mil or 210-466-3015, if you believe that this action is unreasonably restricting competition. Include the subject of the acquisition, this announcement, and the MICC POC information from the notice on https://sam.gov. Provide the specific aspects that unreasonably restrict competition and the rationale for such conclusion.

title: Multi-Ship Sustainment Partnership (MSSP) Single Award Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (SA-IDIQ) Contracts for Fleet Maintenance Availabilities and Incremental Selected Restricted Availabilities on DDG-51 Class Ships Homeported in Norfolk, VA
description: Portfolio Acquisition Executive Maritime (PAEM) is issuing solicitation N00024-26-R-4439 to procure a series of Multiple Ship Sustainment Partnership (MSSP) Single Award Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (SA-IDIQ) Contracts to complete Fleet Maintenance Availabilities and Incremental Selected Restricted Availabilities (ISRAs) on DDG-51 Class ships homeported in Norfolk, VA. Fixed Price with Award Fees (FPAF) Contracts will be awarded across Facilitized and Non-Facilitized Lots. Facilitized Lot includes Fleet Maintenance Availabilities and CNO scheduled ISRAs, to be completed on specific DDG-51 class ships that are scheduled to complete ISRAs over the MSSP period of performance. The scope of this lot includes all efforts necessary to support continuous coordination, planning and preparation between contractor and government to complete Fleet Maintenance Availabilities and ISRAs including, but not limited to, inter-availability preparation and administration (IAPA) support, inspections and assessments, engineering and design support, specification and other government furnished information reviews, and material procurement and logistics support. Unless otherwise specified in a Delivery Order Solicitation, all delivery orders for Fleet Maintenance Availabilities will be performed at the Government facility and all ISRAs will be performed in-plant at a Contactor-provided facility. The Navy will solicit this Lot on a full and open basis. The Navy intends to award up to three (3) Facilitized Lot contracts. The number will be determined at contract award based on the number of acceptable proposals received. Non-Facilitized Lot includes Fleet Maintenance Availabilities only, to be completed on specific DDG-51 class ships that are not scheduled to complete ISRAs over the MSSP period of performance. The scope of this lot includes all efforts necessary to support continuous coordination, planning and preparation between contractor and government to complete Fleet Maintenance Availabilities including, but not limited to, IAPA support, inspections and assessments, engineering and design support, specification and other government furnished information reviews, and material procurement and logistics support. Unless otherwise specified in a Delivery Order Solicitation, all Delivery Orders will be performed at the Governments facility. The Navy will solicit this Lot as a Small Business Set Aside. The Navy intends to award up to three (3) Non-Facilitized Lot contracts. The number will be determined at contract award based on the number of acceptable proposals received. Each contract will include three (3) one-year ordering periods. The supply being procured is the repaired, mission-ready vessel, which is returned to service within the Fleet. This solicitation is issued electronically via PIEE and interested offerors should monitor PIEE and SAM.gov for any applicable solicitation amendments, thereafter. This posting does not include all relevant attachments. Potential offerors will need to request access to the attachments by providing a written request to the Contract Specialist, Alicia Vesey, at alicia.m.vesey.civ@us.navy.mil and the Contracting Officer, Paul Kang, at paul.k.kang.civ@us.navy.mil. Include your company SAM UEI number with the request so contractor status can be confirmed in the System for Award Management. These attachments will be transmitted via DoD SAFE. To receive access to Attachment J-2 (Work Item Plans, Drawings and Other References}, including references that contain limiting distribution statements, provide a written request to the Mid-Atlantic Regional Maintenance Center (MARMC) Technical Librarian, Timothy Russell at timothy.russell1.civ@us.navy.mil with a copy to the Contract Specialist and the Contracting Officer listed above. Include your company SAM UEI number with the request so that contractor status can be confirmed in the System for Award Management.

title: Investigation, Repairs, and Removal and Disposal of Marine Attachments to Raw Water Intake
description: THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL, REQUEST FOR QUOTE, OR INVITATION FOR BID. THERE WILL NOT BE A SOLICITATION, SPECIFICATIONS OR DRAWINGS AVAILABLE AT THIS TIME. The Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command, Mid-Atlantic is seeking eligible small business firms capable of performing investigation and repair services as well as removal and disposal of all Zebra Mussels and marine deposits attached to the active Raw Water Intake (RWI) and associated timber crib structure at Naval Station Great Lakes, Great Lakes, IL. The following are specialty qualifications necessary to perform this work: The Project Manager shall supervise a qualified crew of divers throughout the duration of this contract. Boat operators shall have completed a boaters safety course and have a valid Boating Safety Certificate. Divers shall have a minimum of one-year commercial diving experience in the applicable position; divers shall have completed at least four (4) working dives with similar decompression techniques, diving techniques, and equipment utilized under this contract. Divers shall demonstrate that at least one (1) of the four (4) qualified dives were performed in the last six (6) months prior to the contract award date. Each dive team member shall have a current certification in CPR, first aid, use of emergency oxygen systems, and all other applicable qualifications listed in the OSHA 29 CFR 1910.410. This is a Sources Sought Synopsis announcement, a market survey for information to be used for preliminary planning purposes. Design Build will include the Contractor providing both the design and construction services for a project; during the Design-Build process, final design solutions are provided by the Contractor, not the Government. The Government will provide the SOW, drawings, and other documents as necessary to establish requirements to complete the project. These documents will be equivalent to a design submittal 35% to 65%. When awarded the TO the Contractor will complete any additional design efforts required by the project and produce a set of working documents for use during construction. Construction only method will include the Government providing 100% design package, including the SOW, drawings, specification, and any other documents as necessary to establish requirements for the work to be accomplished. When awarded the TO the Contractor shall commence with construction in accordance with the design and contract requirements. The Contractor is required to furnish all materials, labor, plant, tools, transportation, equipment, testing services, quality control, and incidentals necessary to provide a complete useable end product as specified in the TO/project documents. description: This is a request for information (RFI) / SOURCES SOUGHT SYNOPSIS. This request is not a solicitation (Request for Proposal or Request for Quotations) or a promise to issue a solicitation in the future. Responses to this notice are not considered offers and cannot be accepted by the government to form a binding contract. The purpose of this request for information is in support of market research being conducted by the Air Force Metrology Calibration Program (AFMETCAL) to identify potential sources and gather information on current capabilities within the market. This synopsis is for planning purposes only and is NOT to be construed as a commitment by the Government nor will the Government pay for information solicited hereunder. All costs associated with responding to this RFI will be solely at the responding party's expense. The level of security clearance and amount of foreign participation in this requirement has not been determined. All information received in response to this RFI that is marked PROPRIETARY will be handled accordingly. Proprietary information will be safeguarded in accordance with the applicable Government regulations. Proprietary information or trade secrets should be clearly identified. If, after reviewing these documents, you desire to participate in the market research, you should provide documentation that supports your company's capability in meeting these requirements. Failure to provide documentation may result in the government being unable to adequately assess your capabilities. If you lack sufficient experience in a particular area, please provide details explaining how you would overcome the lack of experience/capabilities in order to perform that portion of the requirement (i.e., teaming, subcontracting, etc.) Both large and small businesses are encouraged to participate in this Market Research. title: Process Gases, Hill Air Force Base
description: Seeking information from interested Contractors for market research purposes regarding the availability and capability of Contractors to provide various compressed gases, cryogenic fluids, and related services for the Ogden Air Logistics Complex (OO-ALC) at Hill Air Force Base (HAFB), Utah. The OO-ALC requires a five-year Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) for the delivery of various process gases to various areas on base. These gases and cryogenic fluids are critical for supporting calibrations, equipment testing, various industrial workload processes, and laboratory testing for all weapon systems maintained or repaired at Hill AFB. The contractor shall provide all necessary labor, tools, equipment, and transportation to perform on-call delivery, bulk refill, microbulk tank refills, and exchange of gas cylinders as listed in Appendix B of the Statement of Work. In general, the requirement encompasses the furnishing of various industrial and specialty process gases (to include, but not limited to, high-purity and ultra-high-purity gases commonly used in industrial, laboratory, and manufacturing processes), associated cylinders or containers, delivery services, cylinder management, and related support services as further defined in the Statement of Work. Please review the sources sought document attached and provide the information requested therein in your response. See the attached Statement of Work and list of gases to understand the requirement.

title: Hubble Space Telescope (HST) Servicing
description: THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. NO PROPOSALS ARE TO BE SUBMITTED IN RESPONSE TO THIS NOTICE. This notice is issued by the NASA/Goddard Space Flight Center (GSFC) to post a Request for Information to solicit responses from interested parties. This document is for information and planning purposes and to allow industry the opportunity to verify reasonableness and feasibility of the requirement, as well as promote competition. Background: The Hubble Space Telescope (HST) remains a top astrophysical research facility in high demand (over 7:1 oversubscription) with 1000+ scientific papers a year (and growing), complementing the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), the Roman Space Telescope (RST), and other observatories, with no replacement expected before ~2040. Hubble�s unique UV/optical capabilities provide critical insights across the entire field of astrophysics, including solar system dynamics, the formation of other planetary systems, exoplanet atmospheres, cataclysmic phenomena throughout the universe, temperature and chemistry throughout and between galaxies, the life cycles of stars and evolution of galaxies. Extending the scientific life of HST will extend the availability of its unique capabilities until the potential replacement, Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO), is operational. In addition, an on-orbit servicing activity to enhance the performance of the observatory or increase its resilience to the effects of aging will help minimize or eliminate the time gap between the existence of the HST capabilities and those of HWO. Lifetime analysis performed in July 2026 identified a 10% probability of reentry by September 2032, and 50% probability by December 2033. HST does not have a propulsion system and, without a servicing action, will ultimately experience an uncontrolled reentry. Mission Options NASA/ Goddard Space Flight Center (GSFC) is hereby soliciting information from potential sources for a potential requirement for orbital altitude increase, on-orbit servicing, and/or orbital disposal or controlled reentry for the Hubble Space Telescope (HST). Information is sought about current and near-term capabilities to perform one or more of the following mission options: Develop, test, and operate a servicing vehicle capable of capturing the HST in low earth orbit and boosting it to at least 600 km Develop, test, and operate a servicing mission to HST to enhance its ongoing performance and increase its resilience and expected on-orbit lifetime Develop, test, and operate a mission to HST to perform a controlled reentry disposal. The requirement includes that the boost and/or servicing mission must not harm the HST and that this mission is expected to occur by 2032. GSFC would provide technical information about the HST, technical consultation with GSFC HST experts, and coordinated HST operations to facilitate rendezvous, capture, boost, servicing, and/or controlled reentry. The contractor would be expected to provide all other resources (including the launch vehicle, spacecraft, crew if applicable, and servicing vehicle mission operations) to successfully perform the mission. This RFI is not to be construed as a commitment by the Government, nor will the Government pay for the information submitted in response. The Government may not respond to questions/concerns submitted. The Government will use the information to finalize the RFP as necessary. RESPONSES As part of your response, please indicate your level of interest in responding to a potential solicitation for this requirement. Interested offerors shall address any or all mission options stated above with the following requirements. Your response should include, at a minimum: Describe your ability to fully perform the mission option(s). Responses should include: Name of submitter and contact information (institutional affiliation, E-mail address). Description of your ability to fully perform any or all mission options stated above Description of your current level of experience or qualifications for each mission option by providing objective evidence of that experience or qualifications (specific but brief examples that clearly indicate the specific experience or qualifications). If you are unable to fully perform an activity, identify such is the case, and address how you may accommodate the area(s) that you cannot currently perform. The technical objectives of the envisioned demonstration. Description of the concept of operations and timeline for mission concept and completion Technical approach(es) for launch, rendezvous with and capture of HST and the current technology readiness level (TRL) of key components, Length of period docked with HST Control of the combined vehicle stack If boosting, amount of boost expected to be obtained, and the minimum altitude of HST that the service can be performed to achieve a boost to at least 600 km An assessment of the mission risk and risk to HST and risk mitigation measures. The earliest date you will be able to perform the service, The maximum HST body rates that can be accommodated during capture. An estimate of cost, payment schedule, and assumptions about your access to government facilities. A description of the monetary and non-monetary contributions/resources the respondent expects to need from NASA. A list of potential partners, including international partners, if any. Your business size and socioeconomic status under applicable NAICS codes. Respondents are requested to provide informed input on realistic and appropriate SB subcontracting and/or participation goals for the specific requirement. This type of feedback supports NASA�s market research and helps ensure the acquisition strategy is aligned with actual industry capability. Industry feedback is requested for: SB Subcontracting goals; Barriers that may limit SB participation, such as certifications, unique technical requirements, security needs, specialized tools, or high-risk performance areas and/or Strategies to increase SB participation, including: Breaking requirements into smaller components Identifying areas appropriate for subcontracting Considering teaming or mentor prot�g� approaches All comments or questions must be submitted electronically via email to Raymond Jones at Raymond.R.Jones@nasa.gov, no later than November 30, 2026 at 3 p.m. eastern standard time (EST). When responding reference 80GSFC27RFIHSTS. All responses should be submitted as a PDF file, 12-point Times New Roman font where paragraphed, as well as single spaced pages with one-inch margins, No more than 25 pages in length.. Files should not be password protected. Respondents may not submit export-controlled information, including International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) and the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) restricted information, in response to this RFI. If a respondent submits confidential and/or proprietary information in its response to this RFI, the respondent must clearly mark the information accordingly. Because the purpose of this RFI is to gain awareness of commercial capabilities to boost on-orbit satellites, if a respondent chooses to submit confidential or proprietary information, the respondent agrees that the Government may use that information for future planning purposes. Any public discussion of the results of this RFI may disclose information about the identities of the respondents. NASA Clause 1852.215-84, Ombudsman, is applicable. The Center Ombudsman for this acquisition can be found at: https://www.hq.nasa.gov/office/procurement/regs/Procurement-Ombuds-Comp-Advocate-Listing.pdf If a solicitation is released, then it and any additional documents will be available on Sam.gov. It is the offeror's responsibility to monitor this website for the release of the solicitation and amendments (if any). Potential offerors will be responsible for downloading their own copy of the solicitation and amendments, if any.

title: Government-Owned, Contactor-Operated (GOCO) and Contractor-Owned/Contractor-Operated (COCO) fuel services at Marine Corps Air Ground Combat Center 29 Palms, CA
description: SOLICITATION SPE603-26-R-0543 Government-Owned, Contactor-Operated (GOCO) and Contractor-Owned/Contractor-Operated (COCO) fuel services at Marine Corps Air Ground Combat Center 29 Palms, CA Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) - Energy - FESAB is issuing a Request for Proposal (RFP) for Government-Owned, Contractor-Operated (GOCO) and Contractor Owned, Contractor-Operated (COCO) Fuel Storage, Operations, and Distribution services at Marine Corps Air Ground Combat Center (MCAGCC) 29 Palms, CA. The Contractor will be responsible for the management, operation, maintenance, product quality surveillance, inventory control and accounting, security, safety, and environmental protection of the Marine Corps GOCO and COCO fuel facilities. The Contractor will ensure safe, accurate, and timely handling, quality control, and accountability of all Defense Wide Working Capital Fund (DWWCF)-owned petroleum products under their control. The Contractor will perform required maintenance to ensure facilities, associated systems, vehicles, and equipment remain operational to meet the base mission. The Contractor will comply with environmental protection, safety, and security directives. The Contractor will conduct required training to ensure personnel are fully qualified to perform Performance Work Statement (PWS) tasks. The contractor must receive, maintain, store, sample and test, internal transfer, and issue petroleum products. The contractor must be responsible for all fuel-servicing operations and safeguarding facilities, equipment, and fuel products under its control during normal and adverse conditions. The contractor must track aviation fuels inventories and order products as needed to meet DLA Energy Accounting Policies and maintain levels to ensure uninterrupted service. This procurement is 100% set aside for Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Business (SDVOSB) under NAICS code 493190 (Other Warehouse and Storage). The Government anticipates awarding a firm fixed-price contract. The Period of Performance (PoP) will be from March 15, 2028 � September 14, 2031 (COCO PoP 3.5-yearbase), September 15, 2028 � September 14, 2031 (GOCO PoP 3-year base), four, five-year option periods from September 15, 2031 � September 14, 2036 (1st Option); September 15,2036 � September 14, 2041 (2nd Option); September 15, 2041 � September 14, 2046 (3rdOption); September 15, 2046 � September 14, 2051 (4th Option), one, 4.5-year option period from September 15, 2051 - March 14, 2056 (5th Option); and an option to extend the contract not to exceed six (6) months from March 15, 2056 through September 14, 2056. This procurement will be solicited under full and open competition after exclusion of sources in accordance with FAR 6.206, Set-Asides for service-disabled veteran-owned small business (SDVOSB) concerns eligible under the SDVOSB Program and FAR 19.14, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business Program. Interested companies responding to the solicitation will be required to register in the System for Award Management (SAM) and Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE). title: Experimental and Mathematical Biomechanics Injury Research IDIQ
description: The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) is committed to saving lives, preventing injuries, and reducing traffic-related health care and economic costs. As part of that mission, the Office of Vehicle Safety Research (OVSR) supports a robust scientific research program to provide the technical foundation for NHTSA�s vehicle and traffic safety initiatives. This procurement seeks to establish an Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract to support NHTSA�s Experimental and Mathematical Biomechanics Injury Research (EMBIR) program. The IDIQ will enable the issuance of Task Orders (TOs) that require a broad range of specialized research, analysis, and technical support services related to human injury mechanisms and prevention in motor vehicle crashes. The contractor shall provide services across the following four research domains: Experimental Biomechanics: Conduct physical testing to evaluate human injury tolerance under crashrelevant loading conditions and identify the mechanisms and thresholds for injury. 1.Anthropomorphic Test Device (ATD) Support: Provide technical expertise to develop and assess ATDs, ensuring biofidelity, durability, and measurement accuracy. 2.Computational Modeling: Develop and utilize advanced computational models (e.g., finite element models of the human body and ATDs) to simulate crash scenarios, validate injury mechanisms, and support virtual testing environments. 3.Crash and Injury Data Analysis: Analyze real-world crash data, ATD testing, and experimental research to support injury criteria development, identify emerging crash trends, and enhance vehicle safety metrics. Data science tools such as AI/machine learning may be applied to enhance insights from large-scale datasets.

description: 539-23-101 Modernize Nurse Call Statement of Work The Contractor shall provide all tools, equipment, material, permits, labor, and supervision required to completely perform the required construction work for the Modernize Nurse Call Project (539-23-101) All work shall be completed in accordance with the project drawings and specifications. The scope of work involves renovation for nurse call system in the main hospital and CLC at the VA Cincinnati Site. Work includes, but is not limited to, general construction, alterations, electrical, and telecommunications necessary for demolition and removal of existing nurse call completion and installation of new work. A full list of requirements and further details are provided in the project drawings and specifications. The above construction Statement of Work (SOW) constitutes a basic outline of work and in no way outlines all details for the construction of this project. It is recommended that a detailed inspection of the premises, drawings and specifications be initiated to determine the needs and conditions for the construction of this project.

The proposed procurement is for services that the Government intends to solicit and negotiate with only one source under the authority of FAR 6.302-1(a)(2)(iii). DLA Energy plans to extend the current firm-fixed-price contract to the incumbent for a period of three months and three, one-month options periods, to be exercised at a later date, if necessary. The performance period will be April 1, 2027, through June 30, 2027 and July 1, 2027 through September 30, 2027, if exercised. The contract will be subject to FAR 52.222-41 Service Contract Labor Standards. DLA Energy, Bulk Petroleum Services Business Unit-FESAB has a current contract in place to provide Government-Owned Contractor-Operated (GOCO) Aircraft Fuel & Ground Fuel Support Services and Fuel Storage and Distribution at Naval Air Station (NAS) Kingsville, Texas to provide services to perform the management, operation, maintenance, product quality surveillance, inventory control and accounting, security, safety, and environmental protection of the fuel facilities.

title: Epinephrine Injector
description: The Defense Logistics Agency is issuing a solicitation for a national requirements contract for Epinephrine Injectors. Procurement details follow. Epinephrine 0.3 MG/0.3 ML Injection, Auto-Injector 2S in 2 count bottles. This will be an unrestricted and fully competitive acquisition. The contract will be a firm-fixed price, requirements type contract with a one-year base and four one-year options. A contract resulting from this solicitation will establish a national supply source, in accordance with FAR 52.216-21 (Requirements), to provide the items listed in the schedule for purchase by Department of Defense, Department of Veterans Affairs, Indian Health Service and Bureau of Prisons customers through the DLA and VA prime vendor programs. The annual usage estimates will be provided in the Schedule of Supplies section of the solicitation. This is a commercial item and will be solicited using FAR part 12. All sources may submit a proposal which shall be considered by the agency. A copy of the solicitation will be posted to the DLA Bid Board System (DIBBS) at https://www.dibbs.bsm.dla.mil and Sam.Gov at https://sam.gov. Interested parties should contact Jeremy Brown at (445) 737-5419, (jeremy.brown@dla.mil) for any questions/comments. Interested parties are further advised to set up automated notifications of pre-solicitation or solicitation changes through this website. The current solicitation date is October of 2026.

The most probable causes of contamination are direct-connected manometers, mercury vacuum pumps, mercury seals, or the handling of mercury in the immediate vicinity. Mercury switches, mercury in glass thermometers, standard cells and other items containing mercury may be used if they are located so as not to constitute a contamination hazard. If external contamination by metallic mercury occurs or is suspected, the following test may be used to determine whether contamination by metallic mercury exists or whether corrective cleaning measures have been effective.
